references.note: The infinite family C(F_{2i+2}F_{2i+3}, F_{2i}F_{2i+3}) = C(F_{2i+2}F_{2i+3}−1, F_{2i}F_{2i+3}+1); rediscovered by Singmaster (1975) and Tovey (1985).

summary: Open. This is de Weger's 1997 conjecture on binomial collisions, in the exact form of Conjecture 2.1 of Blokhuis–Brouwer–de Weger (2017): every collision C(n,k) = C(m,l) with 2 ≤ k ≤ n/2, 2 ≤ l ≤ m/2, k < l is one of the eight sporadic quadruples (values 120, 210, 1540, 7140, 11628, 24310 and 3003 = C(78,2) = C(15,5) = C(14,6)) or lies in Lind's Fibonacci family. What is proved (BBdW Thm 2.2 and the papers it collects: Avanesov 1966 for (2,3); Pintér 1995 and de Weger 1996 for (2,4); Bugeaud–Mignotte–Siksek–Stoll–Tengely 2008 for (2,5); Stroeker–de Weger 1999 for (2,6), (2,8), (3,6), (4,6), (4,8); Mordell 1963 for (3,4); Tovey 1985 for the adjacent shape (n−1,k+1); Stroeker–de Weger 1999 for (n−1,k+2) and (n−2,k+1)) covers finitely many pairs (k,l), three adjacent shapes, n ≤ 10^6 and C(n,k) ≤ 10^60; nothing is uniform in (k,l), which is what the statement needs. Siegel's theorem gives finiteness for each fixed pair, ineffectively. The conjecture implies its parent --h2 (MRSTT 2022, Remark 1.5) and in fact Singmaster's conjecture itself with the bound 4 rows per value. Nothing is formalised.
